content: 1. Fluconazole and Siponimod: Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with drugs that moderately inhibit CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 is not recommended. Alternative drugs should be considered. 2. Fluconazole and Sirolimus: Fluconazole increases sirolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Fluconazole and Sotalol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of QT prolongation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Fluconazole and Tazemetostat: Fluconazole increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per dosage modification guidelines. 5. Fluconazole and QT-Prolonging Drugs: Fluconazole, when combined with drugs like tetrabenazine, thioridazine, trazodone, ziprasidone, and others, increases the risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid these combinations or use alternatives. 6. Fluconazole and Tofacitinib: Fluconazole increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 7. Fluconazole and Tolvaptan: Fluconazole increases tolaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Fluconazole and Venetoclax: Fluconazole increases venetoclax levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicities. 9. Fluconazole and Vilazodone: Fluconazole increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If adverse effects occur, reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 10. Fluconazole and Acalabrutinib: Fluconazole increases acalabrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Fluconazole and Albuterol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Fluconazole and Alprazolam: Fluconazole increases alprazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 13. Fluconazole and Amitriptyline: Fluconazole increases amitriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Fluconazole and Amlodipine: Fluconazole increases amlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for side effects. 15. Fluconazole and Apomorphine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Fluconazole and Aripiprazole: Fluconazole increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 17. Fluconazole and Atorvastatin: Fluconazole increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for side effects. 18. Fluconazole and Avanafil: Fluconazole increases avanafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the avanafil dose to 50 mg once every 24 hours when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Fluconazole and Azithromycin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Fluconazole and Bedaquiline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor ECG closely when co-administered. 21. Fluconazole and Belzutifan: Fluconazole increases belzutifan levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor for anemia and hypoxia, and adjust the belzutifan dose as needed. 22. Fluconazole and Brexpiprazole: Fluconazole increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 and strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors. 23. Fluconazole and Buprenorphine: Fluconazole increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of overmedication or withdrawal, and adjust therapy as needed. 24. Fluconazole and Cabazitaxel: Fluconazole increases cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Fluconazole and Carbamazepine: Fluconazole increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 26. Fluconazole and Citalopram: Fluconazole increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Limit the citalopram dose to 20 mg/day to reduce the risk of QT prolongation. ECG monitoring is recommended. 27. Fluconazole and Clobazam: Fluconazole increases clobazam levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Dosage adjustment may be required. 28. Fluconazole and Clopidogrel: Fluconazole may reduce clopidogrel efficacy by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced platelet aggregation. 29. Fluconazole and Clozapine: Fluconazole increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Fluconazole and Conjugated Estrogens: Fluconazole increases conjugated estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 31. Fluconazole and Crizotinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Fluconazole and Daridorexant: Fluconazole increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the daridorexant dose to 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Fluconazole and Dasatinib: Fluconazole increases dasatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 34. Fluconazole and Dexamethasone: Fluconazole increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Fluconazole and Diazepam: Fluconazole increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 36. Fluconazole and Diclofenac: Fluconazole increases diclofenac levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Do not exceed a diclofenac dose of 50 mg twice daily. 37. Fluconazole and Diltiazem: Fluconazole increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Fluconazole and Donepezil: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Fluconazole and Escitalopram: Fluconazole increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Fluconazole and Estradiol: Fluconazole increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 41. Fluconazole and Ethinyl Estradiol: Fluconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Fluconazole and Etoposide: Fluconazole increases etoposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Fluconazole and Fentanyl: Fluconazole increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for respiratory depression. 44. Fluconazole and Fluoxetine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 45. Fluconazole and Fluvoxamine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 46. Fluconazole and Glimepiride/Glipizide/Glyburide: Fluconazole increases the levels of these drugs by inhibiting metabolism. Use caution and monitor for hypoglycemia. 47. Fluconazole and Granisetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Fluconazole and Guanfacine: Fluconazole increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the guanfacine dose to half the recommended dose when co-administered. 49. Fluconazole and Hydrocortisone: Fluconazole increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Fluconazole and Hydroxyzine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Fluconazole and Iloperidone: Fluconazole increases iloperidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 52. Fluconazole and Imipramine: Fluconazole increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Fluconazole and Indacaterol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Fluconazole and Methadone: Fluconazole increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 55. Fluconazole and Midazolam: Fluconazole increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for sedation. 56. Fluconazole and Mirtazapine: Fluconazole increases mirtazapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 57. Fluconazole and Nifedipine: Fluconazole increases nifedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for hypotension. 58. Fluconazole and Omeprazole: Fluconazole increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 59. Fluconazole and Ondansetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Fluconazole and Paroxetine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when fluconazole is co-administered with other medications, particularly those affecting QTc intervals or metabolized by CYP enzymes.
